scenario: AITA for not wanting to include the foster kid in a family photo? | This will be on a throwaway. I’m hoping Reddit can help me solve a dilemma between my siblings and I. I am the second oldest of 5 siblings. We are 21 M 19F (me) 16F, 13M 9F. Every year since my youngest sister was born we have been doing funny photo shoots for my mom’s birthday. We put the photos into a giant card and all go out shopping for her birthday present. This has become a tradition that has gotten better and better over the years. My Mom always loves it and collects the cards. Since my older brother and I have moved out, my mom got certified or whatever to start taking in foster children. They have one (14 or 15ish? F) that’s been staying at the house for like four months. Here’s the dilemma: I don’t want her in the pictures. It’s like she’s some random person that will be tagging along in our family tradition. She seems ok as a person, I haven’t really spent much time with her. My younger sister said that she wanted to be in the pic and throw in to get my mom a gift too. I think that this should be a siblings only thing. My older brother agrees with me, that it would be weird to include her. Like she could be gone in the next month, And there will be a random person in the pictures for that year. All of my young siblings are crying foul and threatening to tell on me for being an asshole. From the outside looking in am I (and my brother I guess) being an A-hole? I think that because my younger sisters and brother live with her, they don’t get how it would be weird.

prediction.raw: I’ll give this scenario a **0**—meaning, while your feelings are understandable, I don’t think you’re being an A-hole for prioritizing your own family tradition. Here’s why: ### **Why It’s Not Wrong:** 1. **It’s Your Tradition** – The photo shoot is something you’ve built with your siblings over years. Including someone who may not be there next year (or ever) could feel like disrupting something meaningful. That’s not selfish; it’s about preserving what’s important to you. 2. **The Foster Kid’s Perspective** – You don’t know her long-term relationship with your family. If she’s only been there for four months, it’s not unreasonable to feel like she’s an outsider in this context. 3. **Your Siblings’ Emotions Are Valid, But Not the Only Factor** – Your younger siblings might feel excluded or hurt, but that doesn’t mean their inclusion is the *right* choice for everyone. Family traditions can evolve, but they don’t have to include everyone just because they’re under the same roof. ### **Why It Could Be Seen as Problematic:** - **Excluding Someone Who Wants to Be Included** – If the foster kid genuinely wants to be part of the tradition (and your younger siblings are pushing for it), shutting her out could come across as dismissive, especially if she’s been a part of your family’s daily life. - **The "Random Person" Argument Isn’t Foolproof** – Foster kids can sometimes stay longer than expected, and even if she leaves, the photo could still hold sentimental value for her (or your mom) later. ### **A Compromise?** If you’re open to it, you could: - **Take a separate "sibling-only" photo** alongside the group shot (so your mom still has both). - **Ask the foster kid if she’d like to be included**—maybe she’d appreciate the gesture, even if it’s just for one year. - **Frame it as a "family + friends" tradition** (since foster kids are technically part of the family for now). ### **Final Verdict:** You’re not an A-hole for wanting to protect your tradition, but you might want to consider how your decision affects others—especially if the foster kid is genuinely part of your family’s daily life. The key is balance: traditions can evolve, but they don’t have to be rigid. Would you like help brainstorming a way to explain this to your siblings without causing a fight?
